key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence degradation in metal halide perovskites from accelerated ageing data, even for unseen samples.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more explainable stability screening of perovskite solar-cell materials, potentially reducing the time and cost of experimental qualification.
method: Collected 167 perovskite samples spanning multiple compositions and crystallinities
Monitored photoluminescence under heat and light stress, yielding 86k+ spectra
Featurized spectra with a physics-informed model and trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM forecaster
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the model generalizes across material groups, outperforms baseline benchmarks, and is evaluated on unseen samples using more than 86,000 PL spectra from 167 materials.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of the accelerated-ageing dataset, so extrapolation to new chemistries or test conditions should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
